protocol_amendment.reason: The exact-commit V13 red-team review found that receipt publication was neither exception-atomic nor attempt-bound, a direct public writer could escape the development root through lexical dot components, a forced direct write could report accepted after observing a wrong-size inode, and the hard-link and receipt-validation controls overstated their independence. It also identified one incorrect filename in the immutable V12 review-provenance record.
changes: Accept only the V14 document schema and reject V1-V13 without row verification.

Bind every completion receipt to a fresh 256-bit publication identifier, the exact destination basename, the development-root-relative destination path, payload byte count, payload SHA-256, experiment, protocol, and its own canonical digest.

Preflight both deterministic destination names before writing. A stale data path or stale receipt prevents retry before a new data path is created; no-overwrite publication remains authoritative under races.

On an ordinary synchronous exception after receipt publication begins, validate the terminal pair against the exact expected publication identifier and payload. Return accepted with a structured reconciliation warning only when that exact pair validates; otherwise preserve the failure.

Enforce output normalization and development-root containment inside every public writer, receipt-path, and publication-status entry point, and reject dot components again inside the descriptor walker.

Treat an observed direct-write nonregular or wrong-size inode as a hard failure. Metadata-access and durability failures may be warnings, but every accepted return still requires a fresh exact final-pair validation.
Add a standalone test-only canonical receipt parser, digest checker, relative-path checker, and payload checker that shares no production publication-status implementation.

Exercise the actual os.link branch on a hard-link-capable temporary filesystem, including successful data and receipt links, temporary-cleanup failure, and exception reconciliation after the receipt link.
Add stale-receipt, simultaneous same-destination, path-escape, exact-attempt reconciliation, and incomplete direct-receipt controls across rename, hard-link, and forced O_EXCL paths.
Preserve the V12 provenance filename correction as a separate immutable record rather than modifying the original record.

Retain the exact completed provenance and predicate vector 480 prime candidates, 112 draws, 336 curve hashes, 218 registered-curve point enumerations, and 4218 predicate hashes for a completed canonical matrix.
Keep every generated curve-family density-row and canonical run budget at zero.
unchanged_mathematical_boundary: The curve grid, predicates, four null replicates, representative compiler, ordering digest, graph object, cap schedule, five-field objective, matched-null thresholds, positive gate, and negative classification remain unchanged.
Exactness remains finite, TOY-EVIDENCE, and MODEL-BOUND to the fixed compiler and order-ideal construction.
The standalone complete five-field semantic oracle remains frozen-B4 only; transient B6 and B8 legacy controls reproduce predecessor values but are not independent five-field oracles.
No relation generation, rank, linear algebra, target descent, fixed-curve preprocessing crossover, rho comparison, exponent, deployment, or ECDLP result is in scope.
residual_external_resource_boundary: Exact-attempt reconciliation covers ordinary synchronous Exception subclasses under available memory. KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit, process termination, power loss, memory exhaustion, and hostile same-process monkeypatching are not converted into success returns.
An unkeyed receipt detects accidental state confusion but is not authentication against a hostile same-user filesystem actor. Data and receipt snapshots are sequential rather than pair-atomic.

A complete matching receipt is a logical content commit, not proof that every fsync succeeded. Structured publication warnings must be preserved by any future runner, and an immutable external artifact store remains a runner obligation.

The hard-link control uses a test-only temporary root because the canonical mounted development root may not support hard links; it proves branch behavior, not compatibility or durability of that mounted filesystem.
The forced ENOTSUP controls establish fallback state transitions, not real-filesystem compatibility or durability.
The one-buffer snapshot and lexical preflight are not CPU, wall-time, peak-RSS, parser-object, allocator-retention, disk, I/O, cache-traffic, or memory-bandwidth guarantees.
Canonical B6 and B8 feasibility, serialized output size, cache occupancy, and role resource use remain unmeasured.

The module-load verifier digest is diagnostic only; a future runner must bind the exact commit, command, environment, immutable paths, hard process limits, publication result, and external resource receipts.
protocol_amendment.required_next_review: Validate and commit one exact V14 snapshot, then obtain fresh independent theory, accounting, and red-team review. Three scoped GO decisions could authorize only a separate hash-complete launch-plan design with hard external resource containment, not execution.
